preamble: Hlonipha (avoidance-speech) substitution: in Nguni, married women avoid words that sound like the names of senior male in-laws, either by swapping sounds or by replacing the word (Herbert 1990, via Wikipedia). It has been argued that hlonipha helped clicks spread into native Nguni words (Sands & Gunnink 2019; Gunnink 2023, cited in Wikipedia). Zulu gcwala 'be full', with a voiced dental click [ᶢǀ], is recorded as the hlonipha form of zala 'be full' < Proto-Bantu *-jíjada. This is lexical replacement, not regular sound change. Only one example is attested, so certainty is 2.
phoneticEffects: Click Insertion, Hlonipha Substitution, Lexical Replacement

examples.note: Wiktionary: 'Hlonipha form of zala'. Xhosa also has gcwala.
